summary: All ten findings confirmed; seven fixes are corrected. /2: display (3) does omit the det E(G) twist (Payne–Willwacher §2.3 states it; M_{1,2} gives χ = 2 untwisted against the true 1, and #M_{1,2}(F_p) = p² was checked by computer), but only the E₁ page over closed strata takes the twist; the boundary point counts over open strata must not. /1: the stacks and the Boggi–Pikaart cover go to StableReductionPartII together with FIX-RT-AREA-etale's edits, with a boundary-strata item kept in route 1. /3: the single owner of Poincaré duality for DM stacks is the one CLP-24/14 follows (preferably the stack Part II proposed by FIX-RT-AREA-etale), not SF.2, whose text does not cover duality. /4: FF.3 is the better owner of the squarefree count, with ST.4 importing it. /5: a separate DM-stack purity item at WC.6. /6: no new item; cite the weight spectral sequence (DWP.8). /7: R(G) is in Tau Ceti already, plethysm and Exp/Log have accepted owners (Z.3, QM.0), and only the infinite-variable symmetric-function ring needs a Part II of SchurWeyl. /10: the value at ∞ is the x^{2g+2} coefficient, and FF.5 already plans the affine count.

findings.reason: What I checked. (a) The other owner. PAPER-YUAN-26 route 10 is a part-ii route, parent tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction, roadmap StableReductionPartII, 'Stable reduction of curves and stable maps, Part II: moduli of curves and stable compactifications'. Its brief says 'Construct M_g, barM_g and their universal curves for g>1 over Z. Prove smoothness, properness, boundary normal crossings ... Construct projective finite scheme covers and the smooth fine full-level moduli with N>=3 invertible'. Items /69, /250, /251 and /252 are 'Moduli stacks and universal curves', 'Stable curve moduli is smooth', 'Properness of stable curve moduli' and 'Normal crossings boundary of stable curve moduli'. Edit 1 ends 'Consumers: L5:alterations, PAPER-LANDESMAN-LITT-24/106 and MotivicStructuresInModuliOfCurves'. The report also says 'Its items CANNING-LARSON-PAYNE-24/2 and BERGSTROM-FABER-PAYNE-24/moduli-stacks are the same objects', yet its Edit 3 changes only PAPER-CANNING-LARSON-PAYNE-24.result.json. So the finding's account of the fix is accurate. (c) The new roadmap. MotivicStructuresInModuliOfCurves was proposed by PAPER-CANNING-LARSON-PAYNE-24 route 1, a 'new' route accepted on 28 September 2026. BFP route 1 only joins it. A grep of every papers/*.result.json finds no third extraction routing to it. It is a roadmap about the cohomology and tautological classes of barM_{g,n}. It is not a moduli-construction roadmap, and after FIX-RT-AREA-etale Edit 3 its brief imports the stacks. (d) The paper's use. BFP item moduli-stacks states Knudsen's theorem for all (g, n): 'smooth and proper DM stacks over Z; boundary ... normal crossings divisor'. The paper uses exactly that: on p. 2 (smooth and proper over Z, for vdBE Theorem 2.1); in Proposition 3.1 applied to barM_{4,n} (p. 6); and on p. 7 ('Since barM_{g',n'} is smooth and proper over Z'), with the normal-crossings compactification behind display (3). It needs g = 0 and g = 1 as well as g > 1: Keel's barM_{0,n}, and barM_{1,11} in the sharpness of Theorem 1.1. Boggi-Pikaart is used on p. 2 (pure Tate) and in Remark 9.4, p. 22, read on the page image: 'The moduli space barM_{g,n} can be realized S_n-equivariantly as the global quotient of a smooth and proper variety X_{g,n} by the action of a finite group H [BP00]'. The twisted forms [X^sigma_{g,n}/H] are built from it. That is a finite level-structure cover of barM_{g,n} itself, the same kind of object as the 'projective finite scheme covers' in YUAN's brief and de Jong's covers in Edit 1, and it says nothing about cohomology. So StableReductionPartII is the right single owner of both items, and BFP route 1's 'Add, after the moduli stacks, boundary strata and vcd layers' and its reason 'The atlas has no moduli of curves' contradict section 15. The extraction (29 September 2026, #4271) and its review both came after YUAN's acceptance (23 September) and after /4 was confirmed (24 September). The review's route 1 reason repeats 'The atlas has no moduli of curves'. Caveats and corrections to the fix. (1) The widening is decided but not yet applied. PAPER-CANNING-LARSON-PAYNE-24 route 1 still reads 'the moduli stacks M_{g,n} and M̄_{g,n} as smooth proper Deligne–Mumford stacks with their boundary stratification by stable graphs'. The paper uses them, so deleting them from the only item that states them breaks coverage (section 16). Split the item instead, as FIX-RT-AREA-etale Edit 2 did for LANDESMAN-LITT-24/106. Keep moduli-stacks with the Knudsen statement: M_{g,n} ⊂ barM_{g,n} for 2g-2+n > 0, smooth and proper DM stacks over Z, boundary a normal-crossings divisor relative to Z, universal curve barM_{g,n+1} -> barM_{g,n}. Move it, together with boggi-pikaart, to the new part-ii route. Create a new item boundary-strata for the stratification by marked dual graphs, M̃_G ≅ (∏_v barM_{g_v,n_v})/Aut(G) and H^•(M̃_G) = (⊗_v H^•(barM_{g_v,n_v}))^{Aut(G)}, with locator §4, Notation 4.1 and the proof of Proposition 4.2, p. 7, and keep it in route 1. (3) The new route. Use the same parent, title and area as YUAN route 10, with this brief: 'This is the pending PAPER-YUAN-26 Part II of the same id; its brief, with the pointed range 2g-2+n > 0 added by FIX-RT-AREA-etale /4, remains binding. This paper needs barM_{g,n} for all 2g-2+n > 0 as a smooth proper DM stack over Z with normal-crossings boundary, and Boggi–Pikaart's S_n-equivariant presentation barM_{g,n} ≅ [X_{g,n}/H] with X_{g,n} smooth and proper and H finite (Compositio 120 (2000)), over the base the source proves; BFP use it over F_q for every q, to define the twisted forms [X^sigma_{g,n}/H]. Export both to MotivicStructuresInModuliOfCurves.' The base ring and projectivity must be taken from BP00 itself: the extraction says 'smooth projective ... over Q', while the paper says 'smooth and proper' and uses it over F_q. For example: {"route": 6, "verdict": "accept", "reason": "Applies confirmed RT-PAPER-BERGSTROM-FABER-PAYNE-24/1 and RT-AREA-etale/4."}. Text read: arXiv:2206.07759v2 (page image the page image of p. 7). The Annals text was not reachable: Project Euclid serves no open PDF and Payne's home page is behind a Cloudflare challenge. So this verdict is scoped to v2, like the extraction. (a) What is printed. The proof of Proposition 4.2 on p. 7 gives M̃_G ≅ (∏_v M̄_{g_v,n_v})/Aut(G) and H^•(M̃_G) = (⊗_v H^•(M̄_{g_v,n_v}))^{Aut(G)}, with constant coefficients. It then says: 'The weight spectral sequence abuts to the compactly supported cohomology of M_{g,n}, collapses at E_2, and has E_1-page given by (3) E_1^{j,k} = ⊕_{|E(G)|=j} H^k(M̃_G).' The same sentence writes M_{g,n} where the compactification is M_{g′,n′} ⊂ M̄_{g′,n′}. (b) The cited source states the twisted form. I downloaded Payne–Willwacher arXiv:2110.05711v1. Its SHA-256 is 8cd8404c…, the same file the red team used. I read §2.3 ('Deligne's weight spectral sequence') in its LaTeX source, weighttwo_v9.tex, lines 855–884. It says: 'The monodromy action on these branches defines a local system of rank j on D̃^j whose determinant is denoted ε^j … E_1^{j,k} ≅ H^k(D̃^j, ε^j) … the local system ε^j is identified with the determinant of the permutation action of Aut(Γ) on E(Γ). Thus, we have E_1^{j,k} ≅ ⊕_{|E(Γ)|=j} (H^k(M̄_Γ) ⊗ det E(Γ))^{Aut(Γ)}. The spectral sequence degenerates at E_2.' The twist is forced. The E_1 page comes from the resolution j_!Q → Q_{M̄} → a_{1*}Q → a_{2*}ε^2 → … . When the boundary has self-intersecting branches, the alternating signs are defined only relative to an ordering of the j branches. PAPER-CANNING-LARSON-PAYNE-24 item /87 also writes the twist. (c) Check of the counterexample (g,n) = (1,2). I enumerated the stable graphs with legs 1 and 2 fixed. With no edges: M̄_{1,2}, whose Betti numbers are 1, 2, 1. With one edge: a genus-0 vertex carrying a loop and both legs, giving M̄_{0,4}/(Z/2), whose invariant cohomology is 1 + L; and the separating graph M̄_{1,1} × M̄_{0,3}, giving 1 + L. With one edge det E(G) is trivial. With two edges: a genus-1 vertex would force a tree with 3 vertices and total valence 2·2 + 2 = 6, but the two genus-0 vertices need 3 each and the genus-1 vertex at least 1, so 7 would be required. Hence h^1 = 1, and there are two genus-0 vertices joined by two edges. That gives exactly two graphs. In (c), the double edge with one leg on each vertex, Aut = Z/2 swaps the edges and so acts by −1 on det E(G). Its vertex product is a point, so the twisted invariants are 0 while the untwisted invariants are Q. In (d), the loop plus bridge, Aut = Z/2 flips the loop and fixes both edges, so det E(G) = +1 and the contribution is Q either way. Then e_c from the twisted page is (1 + 2L + L²) − (2 + 2L) + 1 = L², with χ = 1. The untwisted page gives L² + 1, with χ = 2. The true value: in the Leray sequence of M_{1,2} → M_{1,1}, with fibre E∖O, the only nonconstant term is H^•(M_{1,1}, V_1), and it vanishes because −1 acts by −1. So H^•(M_{1,2}; Q) = Q in degree 0, H_c^• = Q(−2) in degree 4, and χ_c = 1. By computer, I counted the stack M_{1,2} over F_p from short Weierstrass models, each weighted by 1/(p−1). This gives #M_{1,2}(F_p) = p² exactly for p = 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19; the script is a verifier script The strata also add up: q² + (q−1) + q + 1 + 1 = (q+1)² = #M̄_{1,2}. As a further check, the weight-0 row of the twisted page is Q → Q² → Q, and it is exact because (d) degenerates from both one-edge graphs. The untwisted row Q → Q² → Q² cannot be exact, so it would give a weight-0 class in H²_c that does not exist. So (3) as printed is false, and the corrected formula holds. (d) The conclusions are unaffected. Proposition 4.2(1) and (2) use only three facts: odd rows vanish; Frobenius acts on row 2k with eigenvalues p^k; and dim E_1^{j,k} does not depend on p. The twisted term (H^k(∏M̄) ⊗ det E(G))^{Aut(G)} is a Frobenius-stable subspace of H^k(∏M̄) ⊗ (sign line). This holds because Aut(G) acts over Z and Frobenius acts trivially on det E(G). The dimension is fixed by the Aut(G)-character of H^k(∏M̄), which does not depend on p by the equivariant comparison used for Proposition 9.3. Proposition 4.2(3), §9.3 and Proposition 9.6 use the open stratification ∂M̄ = ⊔ M_G with M_G = (∏ M_{g_v,n_v})/Aut(G), and the Getzler–Kapranov sum over the free modular operad. Both correctly take plain invariants. The proof of Corollary 9.5 cites [PW21, §2.3], which has the twist. (e) Not recorded elsewhere. sourceIssues E1–E6 are other misprints, and PAPER-…review.json and REV-PAPER-BERGSTROM-FABER-PAYNE-24.md never mention det, twist or orientation. The kind 'error' is right, not 'misprint': the printed formula explicitly takes plain invariants, and the closing sentence of §4 ('due to the Aut(G)-invariants in (3)') leans on that. 'affects: nothing' is right. Fix. Parts (1) and (2) are right. In (1), keep the item's Galois clause ('in ℓ-adic cohomology after base change to F̄_p it is a spectral sequence of Galois representations, Petersen 2017 Ex. 3.5') and add 'Frobenius acts trivially on det E(G)'. The second half of part (3) is wrong and must be replaced. 'Every graph sum over boundary strata is taken with det E(G)' would corrupt the point counts. Only the E₁ page of the weight spectral sequence carries det E(G): that is, sums over the normalized closed strata M̃_G, the Feynman-transform side. The decomposition of ∂M̄_{g,n} into open strata M_G = (∏_v M_{g_v,n_v})/Aut(G), and the Getzler–Kapranov formula used in Proposition 4.2(3) and Proposition 9.6, take plain Aut(G)-invariants. For example, for (1,2) the boundary count (q+1)² − q² = 2q + 1 needs the double-edge stratum [pt/(Z/2)] to count 1, not 0. The route 1 brief should say exactly this. E7 may also note that the closing sentence of §4 really refers to the open-strata stratification.

The duplication is real, but the proposed owner, SF.2, is the wrong one. What I checked. BFP route 2 (accepted) says 'for WC.2: Poincaré duality in the equivariant, DM-stack form of Remark 9.4'. The item poincare-duality-dm is routed there and ends 'The same holds for the coarse space of a smooth proper DM stack, e.g. M̄_{g,n}'. PAPER-CANNING-LARSON-PAYNE-24/14, 'Poincaré duality on a smooth proper Deligne–Mumford stack' (the cup-product pairing, compatible with Hodge structures and Galois actions), is routed by route 4 to SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2. REV-PAPER-CANNING-LARSON-PAYNE-24 added that route and accepted it (route 4 'accept', commit 80c70779, 28 September 2026). So two accepted routes name different owners for duality on smooth proper DM stacks. Why SF.2 is the wrong single owner. SF.2's atlas text is 'Sites and scheme cohomology ... construct sheaf cohomology, localization, proper/smooth base change and compact support. Integrate CohomologicalPointCounting suppliers and EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves rather than inventing a parallel six-operations API'. RS-25 keeps SF.2 as exactly that, adding 'No independent six-operations theory'. It contains no duality. For schemes, the Frobenius-equivariant Poincaré pairing belongs to EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.2:pairings: 'For smooth separated finite-type X/k, deduce the perfect pairing H_c^i×H^(2d-i)(d)→E; for proper X remove compact support. Prove graded symmetry and Frobenius/Galois equivariance, giving ⟨Fx,Fy⟩=q^d⟨x,y⟩'. WC.2 imports it: WC.2 requires EDC.2 and EDC.8 and says 'Use the actual Frobenius-equivariant pairing'. CLP route 4's premise, 'SF.2 owns ... compact support and duality', is not in the stage text. Putting the stack case in SF.2 would place a generalisation in a roadmap that does not own the base theorem, against section 15. The confirmed RT-AREA-etale/3 also found that EDC is scheme-only. Its fix, FIX-RT-AREA-etale /3 (merged 29 September 2026), proposes EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheavesPartIIStacks as 'the one owner of ℓ-adic sheaf theory on Artin and Deligne–Mumford stacks'. That Part II covers Rf^! and the dualizing complex (ST.1), adic coefficients (ST.2), and the test 'a Deligne–Mumford stack against its coarse space'. Under 'Recommended (maintainer to confirm)', the report says of CANNING-LARSON-PAYNE-24/14: 'Route it to the Part II (ST.1–ST.2)'. The finding's fix goes against that recommendation without mentioning it. The report's supporting claim that SF.2 → … → EDC.2 would close a cycle I could not reproduce on data/atlas.json plus the accepted restructure links, but the ownership argument above does not depend on it. What the BFP item actually states. Remark 9.4 (p. 22, page image): 'equivariant Poincaré duality tells us that P_{V∨}(t) = t^d P_V(t^{-1})'. For schemes this is a point-count consequence of the duality pairing. The G-invariance of the pairing gives H^{2i} ≅ (H^{2d-2i})^∨(−d) as G-representations, and Proposition 9.3 gives P_{V,i} = [H^{2i}:V]. That is of the same kind as WC.2's 'b_i=b_{2d−i} ... polynomial reciprocity identity', so WC.2 is a correct source for the scheme part. Only the DM-stack/coarse-space extension is duplicated. The right fix. (1) Split poincare-duality-dm. (a) The scheme statement (X smooth, proper and irreducible over Z of relative dimension d, with polynomial point count and G acting over Z) stays in route 2 at WC.2, with the note: 'The pairing is EDC.2:pairings; WC.2 derives b_i = b_{2d−i}; G-equivariance by naturality; P_{V,i} = [H^{2i}:V] by Proposition 9.3'. (b) A new item states Poincaré duality, Frobenius- and G-equivariant, for H^•(X_{F̄_q}, Q_ℓ) of a smooth proper DM stack, or of its coarse space (Remark 9.4, second paragraph). This is the same theorem as CLP-24/14, and it gets the same single owner. (2) That owner should be EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheavesPartIIStacks, ST.1–ST.2, importing EDC.2:pairings. Route (b) there through a part-ii route with parent EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves and record a verdict for it. Move CLP-24/14 there as FIX-RT-AREA-etale recommends. Until the maintainer accepts that Part II (LAFFORGUE-18's route 5 has no verdict yet), BFP item (b) should follow whatever CLP-24/14 then cites, so that no third owner appears. (3) Remove 'DM-stack form' from route 2's reason. Remark. With Q_ℓ coefficients the moduli case also reduces to schemes. By Boggi–Pikaart, H^•(M̄_{g,n}) = H^•(X_{g,n})^H, and EDC.2's pairing on X_{g,n} restricts to a perfect pairing on H-invariants, because H preserves the pairing and invariants are exact in characteristic 0.

The duplication is real, but the proposed owner should be FF.3 rather than ST.4. What I checked. The ArithmeticStatistics packet (BP-ArithmeticStatistics, PR #2864, 24 September 2026) has the node ArithmeticStatistics:ST.4/count-of-squarefree-monic-polynomials-over-a-finite-field. Its statement is 'the number s_n of squarefree monic polynomials of degree n over F_q is s_0 = 1, s_1 = q and s_n = q^n − q^{n−1} for n ≥ 2', its proof is g = e²·d with (1 − qt)^{-1} = (1 − qt²)^{-1}S(t), and its implementationStatus is 'unchecked'. PAPER-WOOD-19/89 states the same count, is missing, and is routed to ST.5. PAPER-ELLENBERG-VENKATESH-WESTERLAND-16/89, which gives |S_n| = 2(q^n − q^{n−1}), is routed to ST.0/ST.5. BFP routes its item as missing to FF.3. So three routings of one elementary count coexist, and the duplication is real. The paper (p. 8, text and page image) reads 'any polynomial can be written uniquely as the product of a square-free polynomial and the square of a monic polynomial', giving (q − 1)(q^{2g+2} + q^{2g+1}) = #P_g + #P_{g−1}q + … + #P_0 q^g + (q − 1)q^{g+1}, with #P_0 = q²(q − 1) and #P_g = (q − 1)(q^{2g+2} − q^{2g}). I checked the corollary: (q − 1)(s_{2g+2} + s_{2g+1}) = (q − 1)(q^{2g+2} − q^{2g}) for g ≥ 1, and for g = 0 it gives (q − 1)(s_2 + s_1) = (q − 1)q², which agrees. Which single owner. The finding's description of FF.3 is inaccurate. It says FF.3 'plans algorithms, not this count' and that its nodes are square-free decomposition algorithms. In fact the FF packet (#2910) plans the counting theory of polynomials over F_q in FF.3: FF.3/count-of-irreducible-polynomials, FF.3/gauss-count-formula ('Σ_{d|n} d·Π_F(d) = q^n'), FF.3/moebius-formula-for-irreducible-count, FF.3/prime-polynomial-theorem and FF.3/irreducible-count-with-constant-coefficient. It rests on FF.2/monic-polynomials-of-degree (card = q^n), and its packet summary begins 'FF.3 plans Gauss's product formula and the prime polynomial theorem, square-free ... factorisation'. ArithmeticStatistics consumers already import from there: count-of-irreducible-polynomials names ArithmeticStatisticsPartIIRandomPolynomials as a consumer. The squarefree count is the next identity in that family, S(t) = Z(t)/Z(t²), and it needs only monicOfDegree and unique factorisation. By section 15 ('plan it once ... in the roadmap that owns it: usually the most foundational one'), its owner is FF.3, not a Selmer-group stage. ST.4 is 'Selmer groups and rank bounds'. It requires ST.3, RP.1, SF.3 and Mordell–Weil and Selmer layers, and has 232 transitive ancestors. Making MotivicStructuresInModuliOfCurves (and ST.5's Wood/EVW items) import ST.4 would pull that whole chain in for a two-line count. The edge FF.3 → ST.4 is acyclic: ST.4 does not reach FF.3 in data/atlas.json with the restructure links. The right fix. (1) Keep BFP's squarefree-count in route 4 at FF.3, which is already correct. Replace its note with: 'The monic count s_n (s_0 = 1, s_1 = q, s_n = q^n − q^{n−1}) is FF.3's, next to FF.3/gauss-count-formula; ArithmeticStatistics:ST.4/count-of-squarefree-monic-polynomials-over-a-finite-field duplicates it and should import it; #P_g = (q − 1)(s_{2g+2} + s_{2g+1}).' (2) Tell the maintainer to move the ST.4 node into the FF packet at FF.3 as a node, with ST.4's Bhargava–Shankar use as a prerequisite on it, and to route WOOD-19/89 to FF.3. EVW-16/89 then imports it. If the stage-level weight of FF.3, which sits after FF.2's Weil bounds, is a concern for ST.4, the FF blueprint can put the elementary counts in an FF.3 prefix that does not import FF.2. The owner stays FF. If the maintainer prefers to keep the existing ST.4 node as owner, the finding's fix is the consistent alternative. Either way there must be one owner, and WOOD-19/89 and EVW-16/89 must follow it.

What I checked. Item deligne-purity states purity for X smooth and proper over F_q ('algebraic integers all of whose conjugates have absolute value q^{i/2}') and is planned at WeilConjectures:WC.3. WC.3's atlas text reads 'Import DWP.4's proved purity ... Follow Deligne I (1.7)⇒(1.6)'. DWP.4 is for smooth projective X and says 'General smooth proper nonprojective varieties belong to the later DWP.7 consequence'. So WC.3 covers the projective case only. The proper case is planned in two places. The decomposition node WeilConjectures:WC.6/purity-for-proper-smooth-varieties reads 'Let X_0 be proper and smooth over F_q. Then H^i(X, Q_ℓ) is pure of weight i, and ... det(t·1 − F, H^i) has integer coefficients independent of ℓ ... absolute value q^{i/2}'. The node DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.7/hodge-type-triangles-and-proper-smooth-purity-3-3-7-3-3-11 plans 3.3.9 and '(3.3.11): lisse enters only through Poincaré duality, so it may be replaced by Ra^!Q̄_ℓ = Q̄_ℓ(n)[2n] ... (e.g. étale-local quotients of smooth schemes by finite groups)'. DWP.7's stage text says 'export the smooth proper nonprojective extension used by WC (3.3.9)'. So planned WC.3 is wrong for the stated generality, and [WC.6, DWP.7] is right. (Strictly, WC.3 owns the projective RH statement rather than merely consuming it, but that does not change the conclusion.) The paper needs the DM-stack case. In Proposition 3.1 (p. 6), X is 'a smooth and proper DM stack of relative dimension d over Z_p', and '[vdBE05, Lemma 4.1] tells us that d_i = 0 for all odd i ≥ s'. The extraction's own item vdbe-lemma-4-1 assumes the α_{i,j} are 'the Frobenius eigenvalues on H^i (of weight i)'. Proposition 4.2's proof (p. 7) uses 'Since M̄_{g′,n′} is smooth and proper over Z, it follows that the odd cohomology ... vanishes ... and every eigenvalue ... is p^k', which is vdBE Theorem 2.1 for a DM stack. No item states purity for a DM stack. The mathematics of the proposed extension is correct. For a smooth proper DM stack X over F_q with coarse space π: X → X_c, Rπ_*Q_ℓ = Q_ℓ, because the stabilisers are finite and the coefficients have characteristic 0. X_c is étale-locally U/G with U smooth and G finite, so Ra^!Q_ℓ = Q_ℓ(n)[2n]: Q_ℓ is the G-invariant summand of f_*Q_ℓ for f: U → U/G, whatever p is. Hence 3.3.11 gives purity of H^i(X) = H^i(X_c). Alternatively, a global quotient [Y/H] with Y smooth and proper gives H^i(X) = H^i(Y)^H. Refinements to the fix. (1) Keep deligne-purity as the variety statement, planned ['WeilConjectures:WC.6', 'DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.7']. Do not widen a 'planned' item with a case that neither stage plans: the stack-to-coarse-space comparison and the local quotient structure of the coarse space are not in DWP.7 or WC.6. Corrections.
(1) The red team says FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums plans the count only for elliptic curves. Its packet has two more relevant nodes:
- FF.5/double-cover-point-count: 'Let F be a finite field of odd order q, η = quadraticChar F and g ∈ F[X]. Then #{(x, y) ∈ F² : y² = g(x)} = q + ∑_{x∈F} η(g(x))'. This is the affine count for every g.
- FF.2/kummer-curve-point-count: the degree-one places of F(X)[Y]/(Y^d − g) number the affine solutions plus one, when d | q − 1, g is squarefree and gcd(d, deg g) = 1. With d = 2 this is the case deg f = 2g + 1.
So the only unplanned step is the points at infinity: there are 1 + χ(c) of them, where c is the coefficient of x^{2g+2}. The new item should take FF.5/double-cover-point-count as a prerequisite. Only the projective completion needs a source route, beside that node (add FF.5 to route 4), not beside the elliptic node of FF.3.
(2) 'Evaluation at ∞ through the leading coefficient' is wrong when deg f = 2g + 1. Then C_f has exactly one point at infinity, whereas the leading coefficient would give 1 + χ(f_{2g+1}). The right convention is f(∞) := the coefficient of x^{2g+2}, which is zero when deg f = 2g + 1.
- It is the extraction's own convention in char-sum-interpolation ('via the degree-d coefficient').
- It is the paper's convention. On p. 8, 'evaluating at x = ∞' counts the f ∈ P_g of degree 2g + 2, and I checked (q+1)(q−1)(q^{2g+2} − q^{2g+1}) = q^{2g}·#G(F_q).
- A chart computation confirms it. In P(1,1,g+1) with coordinates (x:z:y), the points with z = 0 are (1:0:y) with y² = c, which gives 1 + χ(c) points. When c = 0 the point (1:0:0) is smooth, since the local equation Y² = F(1,Z) has a nonzero linear term. The singular point (0:0:1) is not on C_f.
Corrected item: for q odd and f ∈ P_g, C_f ⊂ P(1,1,g+1) is smooth and hyperelliptic of genus g; every hyperelliptic curve over F_q is some C_f; and #C_f(F_q) = q + 1 + Σ_{x∈P¹(F_q)} χ(f(x)), with f(∞) := [x^{2g+2}]f.
